entries.title: Rare Breeds Survival Trust — Leicester Longwool
entries.examined: Photo displayed and examined in browser before generation.
entries.use: Hornless pale face, long pale fleece, breed improved by Bakewell in the eighteenth century.
entries.limitation: A current breed photo supplies anatomy and materials, not proof of an exact eighteenth-century phenotype.

entries.title: Leicester Longwool Sheep Breeders Association — breed
entries.examined: Text consulted; browser site certificate prevented photographic consultation, not bypassed.
entries.use: Explicit warning that modern Leicester differs from Bakewell's original improved sheep.

entries.title: York Archaeological Trust — A Guide to Ceramic Building Materials, 2015/36, section 5.5
entries.examined: Text consulted. Direct PDF image rendering failed; plate 41 not claimed as visually inspected.
entries.use: Late-eighteenth-century onwards handmade horseshoe drains on separate flat ceramic soles.

entries.title: Jetstream — History of Drain Tile
entries.examined: Real photograph displayed and examined in browser; first horseshoe example has separate sole.
entries.use: Visual section and matte ceramic form only. Dating supplied by York archaeology, not by this later American display.

entries.title: Science Museum Group — Easton Hydraulic Ram, Montgolfier Pattern
entries.examined: Full drawing visibly examined in browser; caption reads Hydraulic Ram, c.1822.
entries.use: Spherical air chamber, horizontal inlet body, separate waste-valve stem and delivery route.
entries.limitation: Stylized separate apparatus, not copied diagram. No blue section-fill color, measurements or text.

entries.title: CNAM — Catalogue du musée, section C
entries.examined: Text consulted, paragraph on hydraulic ram.
entries.use: First automatic French hydraulic ram by Montgolfier in 1796; water-hammer automatic water lifting.

entries.title: Borgnis — Des machines hydrauliques, 1819, CNAM
entries.examined: Primary historical text consulted. Scan plate navigation failed; no claim of inspecting its plates.
entries.use: Air reservoir, waste and delivery valves, iron and copper materials; confirms early nineteenth-century apparatus.

rejected.title: Appold centrifugal pump 1851
rejected.reason: Too late for the chosen early mechanical irrigation interpretation; not used.

rejected.title: Fawcett & Littledale irrigation pump, 1823, CNAM archival plan
rejected.reason: Metadata examined but actual drawing not available for visual review; not used as image reference.

interpretation: The hydraulic ram is one illustrative example of mechanical water lifting, not a claim that the technology or its rotative steam parent exclusively describes this machine.
